To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BHMT activity can be regulated by the hormones of the endocrine system and the drugs of different groups.

1) glucagon and theobromine increase the activity of betamine-homosystein-methyl transferase; 2) the effect of glucagon is potentiated by theophylline; 3) the activity of the enzyme in the liver mitochondria of newborn rats is higher than in adult rats; 4) dibutyryl adeno-sine-3, 5'-cyclic-phosphate and NaF have a variable effect on the enzyme activity in
glucagon and theobromine stimulate the activity of betamine-homocyctein-methyltransferase, and this effect is mediated by cyclic adenosine 3',5-monophosphate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cyclic-3,5-AMP in the stimulation of the BHMT activity by glucagon and the effect of theophyllene on the enzyme activity.
the role of cyclic adenosin-3',5' monophosphate in the regulation of the BHMT activity.
the role of cyclic-3,5-AMP as a mediator of the stimulating action of glucagon on the BHMT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
theophylline and glucagon stimulate the BHMT activity, the effect of glucagon being potentiated by theophylline.
the BHMT activity of liver tissue is stimulated by theophylline and glucagon, which is mediated by the cyclic adenosine 3',5' monophosphate.
glucagon, theobromine, cyclic AMP and NaF increase the BHMT activity by activating the cyclic-3', 5'-AMP system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

theophylline and glucagon, which are known to be activators of adenylate cyclase, increased the BHMT enzyme activity in liver tissue and that theophyllin and glucagon potentiated the effect on the BHMIT enzyme activity.
glucagon and theobrophiline, acting through the cyclic adenosine 3',5' phosphate, stimulate the BHMT activity.
theophylline and glucagon stimulate the activity of the liver tissue BHMET.
The main takeaway from our work is that
theophylline and glucagon stimulate the BHMT activity, which is accompanied by the increase in the liver cyclic 3', 5'-AMP level.
theophylline can be used as a drug for the correction of the disturbed metabolism of homocysteine, and glucagon--for the stimulation of BHMT synthesis in liver tissue.
theophylline can be used as a tool for studying the regulation of BHMT.
